member.name: T:ConstTypeArgs.Validation.IValidationResults
member.summary: The interface provides information about the validation results for a const type argument.
member.remarks:
A validation is a collection of two or more verification processes which the validation initiates and collects results from. Though verifiers collect their own results from the tests they run, validations determine whether or not the collected results indicate success. Validation results can be cached in order to avoid repeatedly validating the same const type arguments.
Many validations pass if all of their constituent verifications are successful, though some validations may have additional requirements, or may pass if any of their verification succeeds, or even require that all of their verifications fail.
It is up to the consumer to determine how to handle validation results. This could include throwing exceptions, logging warnings, preventing type initialization, using fallback values, or any other action the consumer deems appropriate.

member.name: T:ConstTypeArgs.Validation.IVerificationResults
member.summary: The interface provides information about the results of verifying a const type argument.
member.remarks:
Verifications are individual tests that are run to determine whether or not a const type argument meets specific requirements, producing results indicating success or failure, along with additional information. Verifications can be applied to const type arguments individually, or they can be grouped together as validations for more complex requirements.
The results of a verification can be cached in order to avoid repeatedly verifying the same const type arguments.
